\chapter{Communication Complexity — Balanced Simulation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.DeterministicCC.BalancedSimulation
\section{Overview}

This module establishes the \emph{balanced simulation} theorem for deterministic two-party
communication protocols: every protocol $p$ on inputs $X \times Y$ with output type $\alpha$
admits a simulation $q$ with identical run behavior satisfying
$3^{c(q)} \le 2^{c(q)} \cdot (\#\mathrm{leaves}(p))^{2}$,
where $c(q)$ is the communication complexity of $q$.
The proof proceeds by strong induction on the number of leaves,
splitting the protocol tree at a balanced subprotocol at each step.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Every protocol has at least one leaf]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.numLeaves_pos}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.numLeaves_pos}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.numLeaves, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.shape}
\difficulty{3}
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice)
and $Y$ (Bob) with output type $\alpha$. Then the number of leaves of $p$ — that is, the
number of output nodes in its tree shape — is strictly positive, and so is at least one.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Single-leaf protocols have zero complexity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity_eq_zero_of_numLeaves_eq_one}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity_eq_zero_of_numLeaves_eq_one}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.numLeaves, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.numLeaves_pos, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.shape}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ and $Y$
with output type $\alpha$. If $p$ has exactly one leaf, that is, if the number of output
nodes of $p$ equals $1$, then the communication complexity of $p$ is $0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Balanced split bound on the squared larger part]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.max_sq_le_of_balanced}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.max_sq_le_of_balanced}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $m, n \in \bbn$ satisfy $3m \le 2n$ and $3(n - m) \le 2n$, so that neither of the
two parts $m$ and $n - m$ exceeds two-thirds of $n$. Then
\[
9 \cdot \max\bigl(m^2,\,(n - m)^2\bigr) \le 4 n^2.
\]
\end{lemma}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.balanced_subprotocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity_eq_zero_of_numLeaves_eq_one, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.max_sq_le_of_balanced, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.numLeaves, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.numLeaves_pos, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.prune, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.prune_numLeaves_of_lt, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.prune_run_outside_of_lt, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.reaches, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.subprotocol_run_eq_of_reaches, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.testSubprotocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.testSubprotocol_complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.testSubprotocol_run_inside, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.testSubprotocol_run_outside}
\difficulty{6}
For every deterministic two-party communication protocol $p$ over input types $X$ and
$Y$ with outputs in $\alpha$, there exists a protocol $q$ that computes the same
function — that is, $q$ and $p$ return the same value on every pair of inputs $(x,y)$ —
and whose communication complexity $c(q)$ satisfies
\[
  3^{c(q)} \;\le\; 2^{c(q)} \cdot \ell(p)^{2},
\]
where $\ell(p)$ denotes the number of leaves (output nodes) of $p$.
\end{theorem}
